title: Improving Seated Postural Control in People With Spinal Cord Injury With a Robotic Trunk Support Trainer (TruST)
official: Improving Seated Postural Control in People With Spinal Cord Injury With a Robotic Trunk Support Trainer (TruST)
summary: This study will evaluate the use of the Trunk Support Trainer (TruST) to assess postural control and sitting balance in individuals with spinal cord injury (SCI). The TruST belt will be positioned around the lower thoracic region (T9-T12) and used during a postural star-sitting test designed to quantify participants' independent sitting control and trunk workspace. Participants will perform maximal trunk excursions in eight directions and return to a neutral sitting position without using their hands for support. Testing will be conducted with and without the TruST force field to characterize postural control across conditions, with maximal trunk excursion used as the primary measure of trunk workspace.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age \>18 years
* Diagnosis of spinal cord injury (SCI)
* Chronic SCI, defined as \>1 year post-injury
* Non-ambulatory
* Able to sit unsupported for at least 10 seconds and participate in TruST testing

Exclusion Criteria:

* Current pressure injury that would interfere with safe participation.
* Severe spasticity that would interfere with study procedures.
* Uncontrolled autonomic dysreflexia.
* Significant musculoskeletal limitations or contractures that would prevent completion of the required seated movements or assessments.
* Any medical condition or other limitation that would prevent safe participation in the TruST assessments or training intervention
